title: Finitely presented spaces descend over inverse limits of algebraic-space bases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Local finite presentation and local finite type are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, let $(B_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transitions, and put $B=\varprojlim_i B_i$. For every finitely presented morphism $Z\to B$, there exist $i\in I$, a finitely presented morphism $Z_i\to B_i$, and a $B$-isomorphism $Z_i\times_{B_i}B\cong Z$. For finitely presented spaces $Z_i,W_i$ over one stage $B_i$, every $B$-morphism between their pullbacks descends to a morphism over some $B_j$ with $j\geq i$; two such stage morphisms that become equal over $B$ become equal after pullback to some later common stage. The bases $B_i$ need not be schemes.

source.place: Tag 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), full algebraic-space base statement, object, morphism and equality clauses.

proof.text: Fix $0\in I$ and work on $I_{\ge0}$. This tail has the same limit: a compatible cone on the tail has its component at $a\in I$ obtained by choosing $b\ge a,0$ and composing with $B_b\to B_a$; a common upper bound proves independence. By [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] choose an affine scheme $U_0$ and a representable surjective etale map $U_0\to B_0$. Put $U_i=B_i\times_{B_0}U_0$, $R_i=U_i\times_{B_i}U_i$, and $T_i=U_i\times_{B_i}U_i\times_{B_i}U_i$. The scheme-test assertion of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] makes $R_0,T_0$ schemes. Associating the fibre products identifies $R_i=B_i\times_{B_0}R_0$ and $T_i=B_i\times_{B_0}T_0$. All these identifications are over $B_i$ and retain the projections, diagonal and triple-overlap maps.

source.place: Tag 07SK (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), choice of an affine atlas and its relation; use the triple fibre product as well.

proof.text: The affine scheme $U_0$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $B_0$ is qcqs, [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product] makes $R_0,T_0$ qcqs. The maps $U_i\to U_0$, $R_i\to R_0$, $T_i\to T_0$, and all transition maps are affine base changes. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], $U_i$ is affine and $R_i,T_i$ are qcqs schemes. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], $B$ exists, $B\to B_0$ is affine, and base change to $U_0,R_0,T_0$ gives the respective limits $U,R,T$. Thus $U=B\times_{B_0}U_0$, $R=U\times_BU$, and $T=U\times_BU\times_BU$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], every $U_i\to B_i$ and $U\to B$ is surjective etale. Consequently the three inverse systems of schemes meet every qcqs and affine-transition hypothesis of scheme-base descent; $R_i$ and $T_i$ are not assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 07SK, atlas limit identifications; Tag 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), including arbitrary base change.

proof.text: Let $Z\to B$ be finitely presented. Put $V=Z\times_BU$. By base-change stability in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], $V\to U$ is finitely presented. Apply the object clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] to the qcqs scheme system $(U_i)$ to obtain a finitely presented algebraic space $V_i\to U_i$ with $V_i\times_{U_i}U\simeq V$. The cited node works over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](1)--(3), viewing algebraic spaces over $S$ as algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with a map to $S$ preserves fibre products and surjective etale scheme charts and identifies small etale sites and structure sheaves, hence preserves quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and finite presentation; apply the cited node to the spaces so viewed, and by the equivalence (2) the resulting $V_i\to U_i$ and the isomorphism $V_i\times_{U_i}U\simeq V$ come from spaces and maps over $S$, recovered through $V_i\to U_i\to B_i\to S$. All later pullbacks of $V_i$ and its overlap pullbacks remain finitely presented by the same base-change theorem.

source.place: Tag 07SK, essential surjectivity after passage to the affine atlas; scheme-base form of 07SK applied over U_i.

proof.text: On $R=U\times_BU$, the two pullbacks of $V=Z\times_BU$ have the canonical isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*V\simeq p_2^*V$, given by keeping the $Z$-coordinate. Their models $p_1^*V_i,p_2^*V_i$ are finitely presented over the qcqs schemes $R_i$. Apply the morphism clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] on $(R_j)_{j\ge i}$ to $\theta$ and to $\theta^{-1}$. At a common later stage they are maps $\theta_j,\eta_j$ in opposite directions. Apply its equality clause over the same scheme system to the two identities $\eta\theta=\mathrm{id}$ and $\theta\eta=\mathrm{id}$. After enlargement, $\theta_j$ and $\eta_j$ are inverse. These are applications to morphisms of algebraic spaces over scheme bases, not to scheme-source maps only. Each application of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] in this step is made over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and transported back to $S$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](2), as in step 3.

source.place: Tag 07SK, descend the finite presentation data and their maps; make the inverse equations hold at a finite stage.

proof.text: On $T$ the isomorphism satisfies $p_{23}^*\theta\circ p_{12}^*\theta=p_{13}^*\theta$: both maps keep the $Z$-coordinate and replace the first $U$-coordinate by the third. The two sides at stage $j$ are maps between the same two finitely presented spaces over $T_j$, by base-change stability [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The equality clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] on the qcqs scheme system $(T_k)_{k\ge j}$ makes this cocycle identity hold at some later stage. Its equality clause on $(U_k)$ likewise makes $\Delta^*\theta_j=\mathrm{id}$ hold. Choose a common upper bound for these finitely many enlargements. All equations persist under further pullback. We have therefore obtained an actual descent datum $(V_j,\theta_j)$ along $U_j\to B_j$, rather than just an invertible overlap map. Each application of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] in this step is made over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and transported back to $S$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](2), as in step 3.

source.place: Tag 07SK, finite data and equality descent; the cocycle and identity equations omitted in the presentation argument are made explicit.

proof.text: The singleton $U_j\to B_j$ is an fppf covering by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus](1). Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization] to $(V_j,\theta_j)$. It gives an fppf sheaf $F\to B_j$ with $F\times_{B_j}U_j\simeq V_j$ inducing exactly $\theta_j$. To check algebraicity, use the map $q:V_j\to F$. For any scheme $A$ and section $A\to F$, the sheaf $A\times_FV_j$ is $A\times_{B_j}U_j$, by the displayed local isomorphism. It is a scheme with a surjective etale map to $A$, since $U_j\to B_j$ is representable surjective etale and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] preserves this under base change. By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus](1), its map to $A$ is flat and locally finitely presented. Thus every scheme-test hypothesis of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] holds for $q$, and $F$ is an algebraic space. Denote it by $Z_j$. The sheaf-descent node alone was not used to assert algebraicity.

source.place: Tag 0ADV (lemma-descend-algebraic-space), proof (1), singleton covering; it uses spaces-descent Tag 0ADT and bootstrap Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), condition (3).

proof.text: We verify finite presentation over the space $B_j$ using only scheme-base locality. For any scheme $A\to B_j$, put $Q=A\times_{B_j}U_j$. It is a scheme and $Q\to A$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], hence an fppf covering of schemes by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus](1),(4). The pullback of $Z_j\times_{B_j}A\to A$ to $Q$ is the base change of $V_j\to U_j$, so it is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Apply that node's fppf locality assertion with scheme target $A$: $Z_j\times_{B_j}A\to A$ is finitely presented. No locality assertion with an algebraic-space target has been taken from that node.

source.place: Tag 041V (lemma-descending-property-finite-presentation), applied after every scheme test A -> B_j.

proof.text: It follows that $Z_j\to B_j$ is finitely presented. Quasi-compactness is exactly the conclusion of step 7 for affine tests. For quasi-separatedness let $A\to Z_j\times_{B_j}Z_j$ be any affine scheme test of the relative diagonal. The induced map $A\to B_j$ lets us form $E=Z_j\times_{B_j}A$. The diagonal of $E\to A$ is quasi-compact by step 7. Pull it back along $A\to E\times_AE$ given by the two chosen maps to $Z_j$. This pullback is exactly the tested diagonal of $Z_j\to B_j$, and is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local]. Local finite presentation follows from [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]: choose a scheme atlas of $V_j=Z_j\times_{B_j}U_j$, whose map to the scheme target $U_j$ is locally finitely presented since $V_j\to U_j$ is. Together these are the three defining conditions.

source.place: Tag 041V, expansion of the three defining conditions using scheme tests; quasi-compact base change Tag 03HF.

proof.text: Base change $Z_j$ to $B$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] this is an algebraic space, whose pullback to $U$ is $V$ and whose overlap isomorphism is $\theta$. The given $Z$ has exactly the same datum, by the construction of $\theta$. Full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization], applied to the fppf covering $U\to B$ from [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus](1), gives mutually inverse maps between $Z_j\times_{B_j}B$ and $Z$: the identity on their identified local objects respects $\theta$, and uniqueness makes both composites identities. They are maps over $B$. This proves the object clause.

source.place: Tag 07SK, essential surjectivity: identify the descended space after pullback using its atlas datum.

proof.text: For the morphism clause fix finitely presented spaces $Y_i,W_i$ over $B_i$ and a $B$-map $f:Y\to W$ of their pullbacks. Repeat steps 1--2 on the tail starting at $i$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], their pullbacks $Y_i\times_{B_i}U_i$ and $W_i\times_{B_i}U_i$ are finitely presented over $U_i$. The morphism clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] on $(U_k)$ descends $f|_U$ to a map $g_j$ over $U_j$. On $R_j$ its compatibility with the canonical descent data is the equation $\theta_W\circ p_1^*g_j=p_2^*g_j\circ\theta_Y$. These are maps between finitely presented spaces over $R_j$; they agree over $R$ because $f$ is a map over $B$. The equality clause of the same scheme-base descent node, now on $(R_k)$, makes this equation hold at some later stage $k$. By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus] the atlas $U_k\to B_k$ is fppf. Full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization] then gives a map $Y_k\to W_k$ over $B_k$. Its pullback to $B$ is $f$, since both maps restrict to $f|_U$ and that same full faithfulness over $B$ detects equality. Each application of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] in this step is made over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and transported back to $S$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](2), as in step 3.

source.place: Tag 07SK, full faithfulness paragraph: descend a map on an atlas and descend its overlap compatibility.

proof.text: Finally, put any two stage morphisms in the equality clause over a common stage $i$ by directedness. Their restrictions along $U_i\to B_i$ are maps between finitely presented algebraic spaces over the qcqs scheme $U_i$, by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. If their pullbacks to $B$ agree, their pullbacks to $U$ agree. The equality clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] on $(U_j)_{j\ge i}$ makes the restrictions equal over some $U_j$. Full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization] for the fppf atlas $U_j\to B_j$ supplied by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus] makes the original maps equal over $B_j$. This proves eventual equality and completes all clauses without assuming any $B_i$ is a scheme. Each application of [lem-sfb-fp-space-qcqs-base-limit-descent] in this step is made over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and transported back to $S$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](2), as in step 3.

source.place: Tag 07SK, full faithfulness and essential uniqueness of the descended morphism.

There are no new nodes and no cycle. The route is atlas descent instead of the source's W/R′ presentation, and it is sound.
